newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Bezeq to cut capital spending.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Bezeq to cut capital spending.

text.p: Bezeq Israel Telecom plans to reduce capital spending in coming years because deregulation has caused too much market uncertainty, managing director Yitzhak Kaul said in an interview published on Tuesday.

"The tendency will be to be much more conservative than in the past in the area of investment in order to reduce capital fund-raising," Kaul told the financial daily Globes. "There are (market) developments that we can't evaluate."

Bezeq's revenue stream has grown more uncertain as its monopoly in various services is gradually being whittled away. Earlier this month, the government awarded licences to two consortia to offer overseas phone service in competiton with state-controlled Bezeq.

Kaul said Bezeq might increase capital spending if market conditions justified it. "If occurs in international communications what happened in cellular telephones -- call traffic grows a lot, which is expressed in our results -- we can be more generous," he said.
Bezeq has spent heavily in recent years to upgrade and digitise its network, but capital spending is set to fall to 2.3 billion shekels next year from 3.0 billion shekels in 1996.
Kaul said the one area Bezeq intended to continue investing in heavily was overseas. The company is active in Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union and is a co-bidder on two big Indian projects.

Kaul said he was not opposed in principle to allowing cable television companies to compete with Bezeq in basic telephone service even before the year 2000, but he insisted further market opening had to be accompanied by regulatory reform to give Bezeq more flexibility to compete.
"For every small service (it wants to offer), Bezeq needs to get permission and wait several weeks for an answer," he said.
